statement: The curve $x^{3}+y^{3}=6xy$ is called the folium of Descartes. Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ and hence find the coordinates of the point with $x=y\neq0$ on the curve.
solution: Differentiating implicitly, $3x^{2}+3y^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}=6y+6x\frac{dy}{dx}$, so $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2y-x^{2}}{y^{2}-2x}$. Setting $x=y$ gives $2x^{3}=6x^{2}$, i.e. $x^{2}(x-3)=0$. Since $x\neq0$, $x=3$, so the point is $(3,3)$.
hints: Differentiate both sides implicitly with respect to x.
Substitute x=y into the original equation.
